answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to lock a refundable stake before it may transact, much like a sparrow must gather real twigs before nesting in a meadow. The stake is small for one honest agent but multiplies linearly with every fake identity, so creating thousands of sock puppets becomes prohibitively expensive. At the zenith of activity, the network slashes the stake of any identity caught double-signing or voting twice, turning cheap forgery into a guaranteed loss.
